subject: math
title: Multiplication Facts to 12 × 12
seo_title: Grade 5 Multiplication Facts to 12 × 12 Worksheets with Answer Key (Ontario)
standard_text: Recall and demonstrate multiplication facts from 0 × 0 to 12 × 12, and related division facts
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 math worksheets on multiplication facts to 12 × 12: the 11s and 12s, facts with 0 and 1, strategies, related division facts and word problems with eggs by the dozen. 100 questions with an answer key, following the Ontario curriculum.
key_sub: Split 12 into 10 and 2, or 11 into 10 and 1, then add. Any number times 0 is 0, and any number times 1 stays the same. Every fact gives division facts: 12 × 7 = 84, so 84 ÷ 12 = 7.
body_html:
The 11s and 12s come from the 10s

In Grade 5 you learn every fact from 0 × 0 to 12 × 12. The new ones are the 11s and 12s. Split 12 into 10 + 2. Multiply both parts, then add.

For the 11s, split 11 into 10 + 1: 11 × 8 = 80 + 8 = 88.

Example

12 × 8 = ?

10 × 8 = 80 and 2 × 8 = 16. 80 + 16 = 96.

Answer: 96

Facts with 0 and 1

RuleExample
Any number × 0 = 09 × 0 = 0, 0 × 12 = 0
Any number × 1 = the same number1 × 11 = 11
0 ÷ any number (not 0) = 00 ÷ 8 = 0
A number ÷ 1 = the same number9 ÷ 1 = 9
A number ÷ itself = 112 ÷ 12 = 1

More strategies

FactStrategyExample

Every fact gives division facts

12, 9 and 108 make a fact family: 12 × 9 = 108, 9 × 12 = 108, 108 ÷ 12 = 9 and 108 ÷ 9 = 12. A division fact starts with the biggest number.

Division

96 ÷ 12 = ?

Think: 12 × ? = 96. 12 × 8 = 96.

Answer: 8

Word problem

A farm packs 60 eggs into cartons of 12. How many cartons does it fill?

60 ÷ 12 = ? 12 × 5 = 60.

Answer: 5 cartons

faq.q: What multiplication facts should a Grade 5 student know in Ontario?
faq.a: The Ontario Mathematics Curriculum (2020) asks Grade 5 students to recall the multiplication facts from 0 × 0 to 12 × 12 and the related division facts. The 11s and 12s are new in Grade 5.

faq.q: What is the easiest way to learn the 12 times table?
faq.a: Split 12 into 10 and 2: 12 × 7 = 70 + 14 = 84. You can also double the 6s, because 12 × 7 is double 6 × 7 = 42.

faq.q: Why is any number times 0 equal to 0?
faq.a: 5 × 0 means 5 groups with nothing in them, and 0 × 5 means no groups at all, so both are 0. Any number times 1 stays the same.

faq.q: Do Grade 5 students in Ontario write EQAO?
faq.a: No. Ontario students write the EQAO math assessment in Grade 3 and Grade 6. Knowing the facts to 12 × 12 well in Grade 5 makes multi-digit multiplication, division and fractions easier in Grade 6.

items.e: There are 3 rows with 12 dots in each row. 3 × 12 = 30 + 6 = 36. 15 is 3 + 12, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: How many dots are in this array?
items.e: There are 2 rows with 11 dots in each row. 2 × 11 = 22. 13 is 2 + 11.

items.q:
Skip count by 12s. What comes next?
12, 24, 36, 48, ?
items.e: Each number is 12 more than the one before: 48 + 12 = 60. So 12 × 5 = 60.

items.q:
Skip count by 11s. What comes next?
11, 22, 33, 44, ?
items.e: Each number is 11 more than the one before: 44 + 11 = 55. So 11 × 5 = 55.
11 × 12 = 10 × 12 + 12 = 120 + 12 = 132. 1212 just writes 12 twice; that pattern only works up to 11 × 9.
11 × 8 = 10 × 8 + 8 = 80 + 8 = 88. For 11 × 1 to 11 × 9, the digit is written twice.
11 × 3 = 10 × 3 + 3 = 30 + 3 = 33. For 11 × 1 to 11 × 9, the digit is written twice.
11 × 9 = 10 × 9 + 9 = 90 + 9 = 99. For 11 × 1 to 11 × 9, the digit is written twice.
11 × 6 = 10 × 6 + 6 = 60 + 6 = 66. For 11 × 1 to 11 × 9, the digit is written twice.

items.q: Which number is in the 12s?
items.e: Skip count by 12s: 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, 96. 84 = 12 × 7. 74 and 86 come from adding 70 + 14 or 80 + 16 wrong.

items.q: Which number is in the 11s?

items.e: 9 × 0 means 9 groups of 0. That is 0. The answer is not 9: any number times 0 is 0. 90 is 9 × 10, not 9 × 0.
0 × 12 means 0 groups of 12. That is 0. The answer is not 12: any number times 0 is 0. 120 is 12 × 10, not 12 × 0.
6 × 0 means 6 groups of 0. That is 0. The answer is not 6: any number times 0 is 0. 60 is 6 × 10, not 6 × 0.
10 × 0 means 10 groups of 0. That is 0. The answer is not 10: any number times 0 is 0. 100 is 10 × 10, not 10 × 0.
1 × 8 means 1 group of 8. That is 8. Times 1 keeps the number the same; it does not add 1.
11 × 1 means 11 groups of 1. That is 11. Times 1 keeps the number the same; it does not add 1.
1 × 12 means 1 group of 12. That is 12. Times 1 keeps the number the same; it does not add 1.
7 × 1 means 7 groups of 1. That is 7. Times 1 keeps the number the same; it does not add 1.

items.q: Any number times 0 equals ___.
c: the number with a 0 after it
items.e: No groups, or groups with nothing in them, make 0. 7 × 0 = 0 and 0 × 12 = 0. Putting a 0 after the number is the rule for × 10.

items.q: Any number times 1 equals ___.
items.e: One group of a number is just that number, so the answer is the same number. 9 × 1 = 9 and 1 × 12 = 12.
Only 0 times a number makes 0, so ? = 0. 1 × 11 = 11, not 0.
Put 9 into groups of 1: there are 9 groups. 9 ÷ 1 = 9. Check: 1 × 9 = 9.
7 shared into groups of 7 makes 1 group. 7 ÷ 7 = 1. Check: 7 × 1 = 7. 49 is 7 × 7, which multiplies instead of divides.
Any number (not 0) divided by itself is 1. Check: 12 × 1 = 12. 144 is 12 × 12.

items.q: Which number sentence is true?
items.e: 0 shared among 8 groups gives 0 in each group, so 0 ÷ 8 = 0. 8 ÷ 8 = 1 and 8 × 0 = 0.

items.q: Which number sentence is not true?
items.e: 6 × 0 = 6 is wrong: 6 groups of 0 is 0, so 6 × 0 = 0. The other three are true.

items.q: Which has the answer 0?
items.e: 12 × 0 = 0. 12 × 1 = 12, 1 × 1 = 1 and 7 + 0 = 7. Adding 0 keeps the number, but multiplying by 0 gives 0.

items.q: Priya puts 1 granola bar in each of 11 lunch bags. How many granola bars does she use?
items.e: 11 bags with 1 bar in each: 11 × 1 = 11. 12 adds 1 instead of multiplying.

items.q: Owen stacks 7 empty egg cartons. How many eggs are in the cartons?
items.e: The cartons are empty: 7 groups of 0 eggs. 7 × 0 = 0. 84 is 7 × 12, the number of eggs if the cartons were full.
12 is 10 + 2, so 12 × 3 = 30 + 6 = 36. 32 forgets to multiply the 2.
12 is 10 + 2, so 12 × 4 = 40 + 8 = 48. 42 forgets to multiply the 2.
12 is 10 + 2, so 12 × 9 = 90 + 18 = 108. 92 forgets to multiply the 2.
12 is 10 + 2, so 12 × 11 = 110 + 22 = 132. 112 forgets to multiply the 2.

items.q: The grid shows 12 × 5 split into 10 × 5 and 2 × 5. What is 12 × 5?
items.e: The green part is 10 × 5 = 50. The orange part is 2 × 5 = 10. Together: 50 + 10 = 60, so 12 × 5 = 60.

items.q: The grid shows 12 × 6 split into 10 × 6 and 2 × 6. What is 12 × 6?
items.e: The green part is 10 × 6 = 60. The orange part is 2 × 6 = 12. Together: 60 + 12 = 72, so 12 × 6 = 72.

items.q: Which is a correct way to work out 12 × 7?
items.e: Split 12 into 10 and 2 and multiply both parts by 7: 10 × 7 + 2 × 7 = 70 + 14 = 84.

items.q: Which is a correct way to work out 12 × 8?
items.e: Split 12 into 10 and 2 and multiply both parts by 8: 10 × 8 + 2 × 8 = 80 + 16 = 96.

items.q: Which has the same answer as 12 × 9?
6 × 7 = 42. Use it to find 12 × 7.
items.e: 12 is double 6, so 12 × 7 is double 42: 42 + 42 = 84. 74 loses the carried ten.

items.q: 6 × 8 = 48. Use it to find 12 × 8.
items.e: 12 is double 6, so 12 × 8 is double 48: 48 + 48 = 96. 86 loses the carried ten.

items.q: Ava works out 12 × 8 like this: 10 × 8 = 80 and 2 × 8 = 16, so 12 × 8 = 86. What is the correct answer?
items.e: Her steps are right, but 80 + 16 = 96. 86 forgets the ten in 16.

items.q: 10 × 7 = 70. Use it to find 9 × 7.
items.e: 9 × 7 is one group of 7 less than 10 × 7: 70 − 7 = 63. 69 takes away 1 instead of 7.

items.q: 10 × 8 = 80. Use it to find 9 × 8.
items.e: 9 × 8 is one group of 8 less than 10 × 8: 80 − 8 = 72. 79 takes away 1 instead of 8.

items.q: 4 × 7 = 28. Use it to find 8 × 7.
items.e: 8 is double 4, so 8 × 7 is double 28: 28 + 28 = 56. 46 loses the carried ten.
11 groups of 7 is 10 groups of 7 and 1 more group of 7. So ? = 7: 70 + 7 = 77.
12 groups of 8 is 10 groups of 8 and 2 more groups of 8. So ? = 2 × 8 = 16. 2 forgets to multiply by 8.
Ask: 12 times what makes 108? 108 ÷ 12 = 9. Check: 12 × 9 = 108, so ? = 9. 96 is 108 − 12, which subtracts instead of divides.
Use the related multiplication fact: ? = 12 × 6 = 72. Check: 72 ÷ 12 = 6. 18 is 12 + 6 and 2 is 12 ÷ 6.

items.q: 12 × 7 = 84. Which division fact is also true?
items.e: 7, 12 and 84 make a fact family: 12 × 7 = 84, so 84 ÷ 7 = 12 and 84 ÷ 12 = 7. Division starts with the biggest number, 84.

items.q: Which fact helps you work out 108 ÷ 12?
Which fact is not in the fact family for 11, 12 and 132?
items.e: 12 ÷ 11 = 132 is turned around. A division fact starts with the biggest number: 132 ÷ 11 = 12.
11 × 12 = 132, so 132 ÷ 11 = 12 and 132 ÷ 12 = 11. They are in the same fact family.

items.q: 8 × 9 = 72. So what is 72 ÷ 9?

sets.title: Mixed facts and word problems: eggs by the dozen

items.e: 12 × 9 = 90 + 18 = 108. 98 loses the carried ten.

items.q: Each carton holds 12 eggs. How many eggs are there?
items.e: 3 cartons of 12: 3 × 12 = 30 + 6 = 36. 15 is 3 + 12, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: Ethan buys 5 dozen eggs for a pancake breakfast. A dozen is 12. How many eggs is that?
A farm packs 84 eggs into cartons of 12. How many cartons does it fill?
The school kitchen has 144 eggs for a Thanksgiving lunch. How many dozen is that?
items.e: A dozen is 12. 144 ÷ 12 = ? 12 × 12 = 144, so it is 12 dozen.

items.q: Leah buys 3 dozen eggs. She uses 8 eggs to bake muffins. How many eggs are left?
items.e: First 3 × 12 = 36. Then 36 − 8 = 28. 36 forgets the 8 eggs that were used.

items.q: Each carton holds 12 eggs. 5 eggs are cracked. How many eggs are not cracked?
items.e: 4 × 12 = 48 eggs. 48 − 5 = 43. 53 adds the 5 instead of taking it away.

items.q: Each hockey team brings 12 players to the tournament. There are 9 teams. How many players is that?
items.e: 9 × 12 = 90 + 18 = 108. 98 loses the carried ten. 21 is 9 + 12, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: There are 12 months in a year. How many months are in 11 years?
Aiden’s baby sister is 48 months old. How many years old is she?
items.e: There are 12 months in a year. 48 ÷ 12 = ? 12 × 4 = 48, so she is 4 years old.

items.q: A store sells maple syrup in boxes of 12 bottles. It sells 7 boxes. How many bottles is that?
items.e: 7 × 12 = 70 + 14 = 84. 74 loses the carried ten. 72 is 6 × 12.

items.q: A school has 8 soccer teams with 11 players on each team. How many players is that?
items.e: 8 × 11 = 80 + 8 = 88. 19 is 8 + 11, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: Pencils come in packs of 12. The teacher needs 132 pencils. How many packs is that?
items.e: 132 ÷ 12 = ? 12 × 11 = 132, so the teacher needs 11 packs.

items.q: Skating at the rink costs $7 for each student. 12 students go skating. How much do they pay in all?
Chloe shares 72 maple cookies equally among 8 friends. How many cookies does each friend get?
items.e: 72 ÷ 8 = ? Think 8 × ? = 72. 8 × 9 = 72, so each friend gets 9 cookies.

items.q: For the Grade 5 assembly, the gym has 8 rows of chairs with 12 chairs in each row. How many chairs is that?
items.e: 8 × 12 = 80 + 16 = 96. 86 loses the carried ten. 88 is 8 × 11.

items.q: On a canoe trip, 6 groups each carry 12 bottles of water. How many bottles is that?
items.e: 6 × 12 = 60 + 12 = 72. 62 loses the carried ten. 18 is 6 + 12.
